direct_answer: The real local checkpoint already contains a usable single trained full-attention MTP block: 15 BF16 tensors,121656320 bytes. Ordinary target operation support is largely reusable; the current320-tensor text consumer never loads or executes this block.

The shortest truthful first consumer is bounded greedy K=1: one real MTP draft, target verifyT2 with both row decisions/hidden states, actual acceptance0/1 and a checked correction/bonus token. Keep weights/shared plans in one Model; use original Graph/Invocation/Queue for the distinct mathematical roles.

Current whole-candidate commit and last-row-only outputs are the concrete seams. Existing GDN snapshots and atomic state versions cover recurrent selection, but the current paged-ready public API does not expose projection of an existing verified frame to a shorter accepted layout.

A correct initial rejection fallback can retire/abort verification and replay only the accepted target prefix using existingT1. This has real extra cost and must be measured. Local llama.cpp contains actual Qwen MTP code, including in the retained cached source; however the present benchmark GGUF was explicitly exported --no-mtp and has320 tensors/nextn=null. Existing ordinary peer timings are not MTP results.

local_weights.shared: No dedicated MTP embedding or LM-head tensor is in these15; reuse original token embedding/tied LM head. Do not duplicate the target bank.

math_and_alignment: Observed local Qwen MTP graph: independently RMS-normalize shifted target hidden h_p and token embedding e(x_{p+1}); concatenate [embedding_norm,hidden_norm] in that order; apply fc[2048,4096]; one normal gated full-attention decoder block; MTP norm; shared embedding/LM head. It is not an extra GDN layer and not merely another LM-head matmul.

Its attention is Hq8/Hkv2/D256, q_proj includes interleaved Q/gate (4096 outputs), q/k head norm, rotary64 with the original positions/MRoPE convention, sigmoid attention gate, output projection and residual, then norm+SwiGLU6144+residual. Reuse the existing ordinary text operations and declared dtype boundaries.

Raw HF norm parameters are delta weights; current Hyle Recipe.norm explicitly adds1 inF32. Local llama conversion remaps enorm/hnorm/shared_head.norm and adds1 to norm weights, often storing vectorsF32. Never add1 again to already converted GGUF norm values.

Both inspected llama revisions expose target h_nextn after final RMS norm and before LM-head row selection. Hyle already computes that full activation but publishes only its last BF16 row. Prefill MTP catch-up requires all actual rows; the shifted first pair uses saved previous hidden (zero on a new sequence in inspected llama), then each next token pairs with the previous target row.

For more than one speculative step, the same trained head recurs with its own KV and its own predicted normalized hidden. After target verification, carryover hidden must be reset to the actual accepted target row, not the last speculative row. One trained head does not mean an architectural hard limit of one drafted token.

This is a source-defined mathematical route, not a claim of BF16/F32 bit identity across llama and Hyle. The local checkpoint supplies no standalone official MTP forward module here; preserve each chosen reference dtype/cast tree and validate the head numerically before signing acceptance-rate results.

minimal_K1_round.base: Committed target state has processed L tokens; its last hidden h[L-1] and sampled next_id x[L] are available. x[L] was already returned by the previous target step but has not yet been fed into target state; do not count/emit it a second time.
minimal_K1_round.draft: Run real MTP head on (h[L-1], embedding(x[L])) at positionL with its own synchronized KV; propose d1.
minimal_K1_round.verify: Run original24-layer target on [x[L],d1] at positionsL,L+1, publishing both target row IDs/hidden. Compare d1 with row0 greedy ID; row1 is the bonus only when d1 is accepted.
minimal_K1_round.accept: If equal, commit full target candidate after2 processed inputs, emit d1 and row1 bonus, retain actual hidden/state at the end of the accepted prefix; bonus remains pending input for the next round.
minimal_K1_round.reject: If unequal, commit state only after x[L], emit row0 correction and retain its corresponding hidden/state. The rejected d1 is never published as accepted state. First implementation may abort retiredT2 candidate then rerunT1 from the old head; assert the rerun decision equals verify row0.
minimal_K1_round.failure: On verification/native error or cancellation, no accepted head publication. Retain all candidate owners through true retirement; roll back reserved suffix and discard fresh candidate reservations through original APIs before reuse.
minimal_K1_round.policy: Start with deterministic greedy exact-ID matching, not probabilistic rejection. Stochastic MTP additionally needs actual p/q distributions, independent RNG/sampler state, accept min(1,p/q), and normalized max(0,p-q) correction; TopK equality alone does not preserve that distribution.

Accept/reject before visible head commit. Track target state, draft KV/frontier, pending actual hidden, pending token and position as one coherent continuation identity. Draft-only work must not advance target length or toggle its ordinary parity twice.

For K1 keep final-state GDN outputs and on reject abort/retire then replay acceptedT1. This needs no new schema but costs another target forward on rejection; do not advertise efficient partial accept or hide replay in throughput.

Without it, use real replay; neither metadata length nor PageInventory IDs substitute for F1.

Existing fixed teacher-forced decode tape can check numerics but is not an autonomous MTP acceptance-rate benchmark.
